A customizable form may be produced by receiving a form file that includes an acceptability filter and at least one optional form element. The optional element is included in the applicability filter, may be switched on or off, and is associated with one or more defined conditions that determine when it applies within the form file. A configurable form file is then generated.

In a graphical user interface, required form elements may be displayed together with optional elements, with the optional elements appearing according to the conditions established and evaluated through the applicability filter. The disclosure also describes a search list that allows a data source to be designated without writing code.

A configurable form may include an applicability or acceptability filter, as well as optional form items that can be enabled or disabled when defined circumstances are met. outputs.L4:
The disclosure describes a system for creating and operating configurable electronic forms in conjunction with flow-process files. Each form may include mandatory items that are always presented and optional items whose availability or visibility depends on the context in which the form is used. Acceptability and applicability filters evaluate relevant conditions—such as record type, process state, user role, data values, or other contextual information—to determine which forms, form items, actions, and data sources are appropriate for a particular transaction or workflow stage.

Optional form items may be defined independently of the mandatory form structure and incorporated dynamically when their associated criteria are satisfied. As a result, the user interface can present required fields together with only those optional fields that are relevant to the current record or process. Items that do not apply are omitted, hidden, or otherwise made unavailable. This approach allows a single form definition to support multiple scenarios without requiring a separate form for each combination of conditions.

The system may also use configurable, code-free search lists to identify available records, actions, or data sources. Rather than relying on custom program logic, an administrator or other authorized user can define search criteria and filtering rules through configuration data. At runtime, the system evaluates those definitions to locate qualifying records and determine which actions may be performed. Actions associated with matching records can therefore be discovered automatically and exposed through the interface when applicable.

Flow-process files coordinate these elements by defining the relevant workflow, process states, transitions, and associated form behavior. When a user opens or updates a record, the system evaluates the applicable process definition, retrieves the appropriate mandatory and optional form items, applies the configured filters, and generates the resulting interface. The system may repeat this evaluation as record values or process conditions change, allowing the displayed fields, available actions, and selectable data sources to be updated dynamically.

By separating form and workflow behavior from application code, the disclosed approach enables forms and processes to be modified through configuration rather than software development. New optional items, search lists, filtering rules, data sources, and record actions can be added or revised without writing custom code. The resulting interface remains responsive to the current user, record, and process context while reducing duplication, simplifying maintenance, and supporting flexible form behavior across different business scenarios.
outputs.L5:

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a patent disclosure about configurable forms, conditional non-mandatory fields, flow-form process files, automatic action discovery, and code-free data-source selection.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent disclosure describes a configurable, code-free platform for building and executing electronic forms and workflows. Form fields can be displayed, hidden, enabled, or treated as optional based on user input, contextual rules, or process state, allowing conditional non-mandatory fields without custom programming.

Workflow behavior is defined through “flow-form” process files that package form structure, routing logic, actions, and data mappings. The system can automatically discover available actions—such as approvals, transitions, integrations, or submissions—from process definitions and runtime context, then present only applicable options to users.

The platform also enables users to select and bind forms to databases, services, or other data sources through configuration interfaces rather than code. Overall, the invention aims to simplify creation, modification, and deployment of dynamic forms and business processes while reducing reliance on software developers.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention that dynamically displays optional form items based on applicability filters and predefined circumstances.
counterfactuals.output: A computer-implemented system and method dynamically presents optional items in an electronic form based on applicability criteria and predefined circumstances. Form configuration data associates respective optional form items with one or more applicability filters defining conditions under which the items are relevant. During completion of the form, the system receives contextual information, user input, stored data, or combinations thereof, and evaluates the applicability filters against predefined circumstances represented by the received information. Optional form items satisfying the filters are automatically displayed, enabled, or otherwise made available within the form, while nonapplicable items are hidden, disabled, or omitted. The evaluation may be repeated in response to changes in form data or contextual information, thereby updating the displayed items in real time. The disclosed approach reduces form complexity, limits presentation of irrelevant questions or controls, and supports configurable form behavior without requiring modification of underlying application logic.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a system for creating and configuring forms and workflow process files, including auto-discovery of available record actions from files stored in a data store.
counterfactuals.output:
## System Overview

The system is a metadata-driven platform for creating user forms and workflow process definitions. Forms and workflows are stored as versioned files in a data store, while record actions—such as approve, reject, assign, archive, or invoke an external service—are discovered automatically from action-definition files in the same or a related store.

### 1. Main Components

1. **Form Designer**
   - Drag-and-drop editor for fields, sections, validation rules, and conditional visibility.
   - Supports reusable field and layout components.
   - Produces declarative form files in JSON or YAML.
   - Can bind fields to a record type or schema.

2. **Workflow Designer**
   - Graphical or text-based editor for states, transitions, tasks, timers, and decisions.
   - Associates transitions with available record actions.
   - Validates that referenced forms, schemas, and actions exist.
   - Produces declarative workflow process files.

3. **Definition Store**
   - Stores forms, workflows, schemas, and action definitions.
   - May be an object store, source-control repository, database-backed file service, or mounted directory.
   - Supports versioning, environment-specific configuration, and publishing states such as draft, active, and retired.

4. **Definition Registry**
   - Maintains an indexed catalog of definitions discovered in the store.
   - Resolves names and versions.
   - Exposes searchable APIs to designers and runtime services.
   - Records validation and compatibility status.

5. **Workflow Runtime**
   - Creates and advances workflow instances.
   - Renders the appropriate form for the current state or task.
   - Evaluates conditions and permissions.
   - Executes record actions and records execution history.

6. **Action Discovery Service**
   - Scans or watches the data store for action-definition files.
   - Parses, validates, and registers available actions.
   - Removes or deactivates registry entries when source files are deleted or retired.

---

## Suggested File Organization

```text
/definitions
  /schemas
    customer.schema.json
    request.schema.json

  /forms
    request-create.form.yaml
    request-review.form.yaml

  /workflows
    request-approval.workflow.yaml

  /actions
    approve.action.yaml
    reject.action.yaml
    assign.action.yaml
    archive.action.yaml
```

Each file should have a stable identifier and version rather than relying solely on its path.

---

## Form Definition Example

```yaml
kind: Form
id: request-review
version: 2.1.0
recordType: request
title: Review Request

layout:
  type: sections
  sections:
    - title: Request Details
      fields:
        - name: title
          component: text
          readOnly: true

        - name: amount
          component: currency
          readOnly: true

        - name: reviewComment
          component: textarea
          requiredWhen: "record.status == 'UNDER_REVIEW'"

actions:
  source: discovered
  include:
    - request.approve
    - request.reject
  placement: footer
```

The form renderer retrieves the file, resolves the record schema, evaluates visibility and validation expressions, and obtains action metadata from the action registry.

---

## Workflow Definition Example

```yaml
kind: Workflow
id: request-approval
version: 1.4.0
recordType: request
initialState: draft

states:
  draft:
    form: request-create@2
    transitions:
      submit:
        to: under-review
        action: request.submit

  under-review:
    form: request-review@2
    transitions:
      approve:
        to: approved
        action: request.approve
        allowedRoles: [manager]

      reject:
        to: rejected
        action: request.reject
        allowedRoles: [manager]

  approved:
    terminal: true

  rejected:
    terminal: true
```

The workflow compiler verifies that every state, form, transition, and action reference is valid before the workflow can be published.

---

## Record Action Definition

An action file describes an operation that can be applied to a record. It contains enough metadata for both design-time discovery and runtime execution.

```yaml
kind: RecordAction
id: request.approve
version: 1.0.0
displayName: Approve
recordTypes: [request]

availability:
  expression: "record.status == 'UNDER_REVIEW'"
  requiredRoles: [manager]

inputSchema:
  type: object
  properties:
    comment:
      type: string

executor:
  type: http
  method: POST
  endpointRef: approval-service
  path: /requests/{record.id}/approve

effects:
  emits:
    - request.approved

ui:
  style: primary
  confirmation: "Approve this request?"
  order: 10
```

Possible executor types include:

- Internal command or service handler
- HTTP endpoint
- Serverless function
- Message or event publication
- Script executed in a sandbox
- Workflow sub-process

Sensitive values should be referenced through secret or connection identifiers, not embedded in the file.

---

## Auto-Discovery Process

### Initial Scan

On startup or deployment, the discovery service:

1. Enumerates files under configured action paths or prefixes.
2. Selects files matching supported conventions, such as:
   - `*.action.json`
   - `*.action.yaml`
   - Files whose content declares `kind: RecordAction`
3. Parses each file.
4. Validates it against the action-definition schema.
5. Verifies identifiers, versions, executor types, and record-type references.
6. Calculates a content hash.
7. Adds or updates the corresponding registry entry.
8. Marks invalid definitions as unavailable and records diagnostics.

### Incremental Discovery

The service can detect changes through:

- Object-store notifications
- File-system watchers
- Repository webhooks
- Database change feeds
- Scheduled polling using modification time, ETag, or content hash

Events are processed idempotently. A registry entry is updated only if the source revision or hash changes.

### Conflict Handling

If multiple files declare the same action ID and version:

- Reject all conflicting definitions, or
- Apply an explicit precedence policy based on namespace, environment, or store priority

Precedence should never depend on nondeterministic scan order.

### Deletion and Retirement

When a file disappears:

- Mark the corresponding action version as unavailable.
- Do not break already-running workflow instances that are pinned to an immutable version.
- Prevent new forms or workflows from selecting the removed action.
- Optionally retain cached metadata and audit history.

---

## Action Resolution

At design time, the form and workflow designers query the registry:

```http
GET /api/action-definitions?recordType=request&status=active
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "request.approve",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "displayName": "Approve",
      "requiredRoles": ["manager"],
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

At runtime, available actions are filtered according to:

1. Record type
2. Current workflow state
3. Transition configuration
4. Record data and action availability expressions
5. User roles and permissions
6. Tenant or environment
7. Action version and publication status

The server must repeat all authorization and availability checks when an action is invoked; UI filtering alone is not sufficient.

---

## Creation and Publishing Lifecycle

A typical lifecycle is:

1. **Create**
   - Author creates a form or workflow in the designer.
   - The designer saves a draft definition.

2. **Validate**
   - Schema validation is performed.
   - References to fields, forms, workflows, and actions are resolved.
   - Expressions are parsed and type-checked where possible.

3. **Preview and Test**
   - Forms are rendered with sample records.
   - Workflow paths can be simulated.
   - Action executors can be mocked or run in a test environment.

4. **Publish**
   - The definition receives an immutable version.
   - The registry indexes it.
   - Runtime services receive a cache-invalidation event.

5. **Activate**
   - A version or version range becomes the default for new instances.
   - Existing workflow instances remain pinned to their original version.

6. **Retire**
   - New usage is blocked, while historical references remain resolvable.

---

## Runtime Invocation

A record action invocation should include the expected record revision to prevent lost updates:

```http
POST /api/records/req-123/actions/request.approve
If-Match: "record-revision-17"
```

```json
{
  "actionVersion": "1.0.0",
  "workflowInstanceId": "wf-456",
  "input": {
    "comment": "Approved within budget."
  },
  "idempotencyKey": "27d73dc8-..."
}
```

The runtime then:

1. Loads the pinned workflow and action definitions.
2. Authorizes the user.
3. Confirms that the action is valid for the current state.
4. Validates input against the action’s input schema.
5. Executes the configured handler.
6. Updates the record and workflow state transactionally where possible.
7. Emits configured events.
8. Stores a complete audit entry.
9. Returns the updated record and newly available actions.

---

## Operational and Security Requirements

- Sign or approve definitions before production activation.
- Restrict who may create actions, especially script or HTTP executors.
- Use allowlists for executor types, destinations, and expression functions.
- Sandbox custom code with resource and time limits.
- Encrypt the definition store and use least-privilege access.
- Cache compiled definitions, but invalidate them using store events or registry revisions.
- Record discovery failures, publication events, and action executions in an audit log.
- Expose metrics for scan duration, invalid files, registry lag, execution failures, and stale references.
- Pin workflow instances to immutable definition versions to ensure reproducibility.

This architecture separates declarative authoring, discovery, validation, and execution, allowing new record actions to become available to form and workflow designers simply by adding validated action files to the configured data store.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a single-paragraph invention summary covering configurable form files, acceptability or applicability filters, optional fields that can be switched on or off, workflow action discovery, and no-code search-list configuration.
counterfactuals.output: The invention provides a configurable, no-code platform for creating and managing form files in which administrators define data structures, presentation rules, and processing behavior without software development. Acceptability or applicability filters dynamically determine whether forms, sections, fields, records, or actions are valid or relevant based on user attributes, entered data, context, or business rules. Optional fields may be selectively switched on or off globally, by configuration, or at runtime, enabling a single form definition to support multiple use cases. The platform further discovers and presents available workflow actions according to the current record state, user permissions, and applicable rules. No-code search-list configuration allows administrators to specify searchable data sources, displayed columns, filters, sorting, and selection behavior, thereby providing adaptable forms, guided workflows, and context-sensitive record lookup through reusable configuration rather than custom code.
